title: Land the raw claims in Bronze
prompt:
The clinic group's insurance claims arrive as one raw export, `claims` below: 2,425 rows straight from the billing system. Look at it first: add `claims.printSchema()` and `print(claims.count())` to your file and press Run.

Bronze is the first layer of the lakehouse: the data exactly as it arrived, plus where it came from. Write `bronze_claims(claims)`. It keeps every row and column unchanged and adds two provenance columns at the end.
rules: Keep every column of `claims`, in its order, with the same values. Every row stays, repeated and broken ones included.
Add `_source_file`, always `claims.csv`, then `_load_month`: the month the claim was submitted, as text like `2026-01`.
hints: `claims.select("*", ...)` keeps every column and adds new ones after them.
`F.lit("claims.csv")` is a fixed value; `F.date_format("submitted_date", "yyyy-MM")` gives the month as text.
`date_format` of a missing date is missing too. `F.coalesce(..., F.lit("unknown"))` fills it.
explanation: Bronze changes nothing and drops nothing, so every later table can be rebuilt from it and every odd row can be traced back. `select("*", ...)` keeps the raw columns in their order and adds the provenance columns at the end, starting with `_` so nobody mistakes them for data. They are plain values worked out from the row itself, never from the clock: a rerun gives the same Bronze table. The load month comes from `submitted_date`, the day the claim reached the billing system, and a claim with no date still lands, marked `unknown`, for the next step to quarantine.
